- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/agent_cli/schemas.rs` (`tool_for`, ~line 71)
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/agent_cli/policy.rs` (tier gating / which `call-*` tools get registered)
- `agent_call.rs`, `agent_read.rs`, and the dispatched app commands under `commands/**`

**Observed** (from an end-to-end run against installed v0.149.0 on Windows 11, server launched read-only via `<exePath> agent mcp` with no allow flags):

> Refusal: `{"detail":"this command is classified for \`call-reversible\`, not \`call-read\` — call it there instead","error":"wrong_tool"}`. But `tools/list` on that launch returns exactly: best-matches, job, profile, automations, found-jobs, commands, call-read. There is no `call-reversible` tool to call.

> The server instructions reinforce the dead end: "A call-\* refusal named `wrong_tool` means retry on the OTHER tool its own detail names" — but at the read tier `call-reversible` is not registered. The assistant obediently went looking for it ("No matching deferred tools found").

Mechanism, confirmed in source: `local_call_refusal(tool_name, verb)` takes no `Tier`. It resolves `right_tool` from a pure effect→name mapping (`tool_for(&entry.effect)`), so the refusal always names the tool that *would* handle the effect, regardless of whether this process registered it. The tier the server was launched at never reaches the message.

**Expected**

When the named tier is not exposed on the current launch, the refusal should say so and name the actionable fix — for example: "this command is Reversible and this server was started without `--allow-reversible`; ask the user to relaunch the server with that flag." The server `instructions` should carry the same caveat rather than unconditionally telling the model to retry on the other `call-*` tool.

**User impact**

The assistant is told, in the app's own words, to retry on a tool the client cannot see. It searches its tool list, finds nothing, and either stalls or reports a vague failure — the user is never told that the actual remedy is a one-flag relaunch of the MCP server (Settings → Developer). A cheap, recoverable situation ("this needs write access") is presented as an unexplained dead end, and the user is left with no way to act on it.

**Suggested fix**

On a read-only launch the refusal should say that the target command needs `--allow-reversible` / `--allow-irreversible` and that the user must relaunch the server with that flag, instead of pointing at a tool the client cannot see. Concretely: pass the active `Tier` into `local_call_refusal`, and when `right_tool` is not registered at that tier, emit a distinct detail (and ideally a distinct `error` sentinel such as `tier_not_enabled`) naming the flag. Mirror the caveat in the server `instructions` text so the model does not treat "retry on the other tool" as unconditional.

**Verification**

Both member findings were reproduced by an independent run (2/2 deterministic: identical refusal text and identical `tools/list` output) and judged against the project's own design docs — the judge classified this as a genuine server-side defect that contradicts the documented intent rather than implementing it. The root cause was additionally confirmed by reading the signature of `local_call_refusal`, which has no tier parameter.

title: agent.query surface lacks the frame-cap refusal and identifier clamp that agent.call now has
body:
The `agent.query` surface (the curated resources: `best-matches`, `job`, `profile`, `automations`, `found-jobs`) has no frame-cap enforcement and echoes caller-supplied identifiers into its refusals without a bound, so an oversized reply or an oversized `resource`/`reqId` still ends as a content-free `connection_lost` on the client.

**Severity**: medium
**Area**: `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/extension_bridge/agent_read.rs` (`handle_agent_query`, `origin_refused_reply`, `throttled_reply`), `extension_bridge/stream.rs` (`spawn_agent_query` writes the result straight to the outbound channel).

**Context**

The generic `agent.call` surface received both controls in the result-cap work: replies are measured against the bridge's `MAX_FRAME_BYTES` and refused as `result_too_large`, and every refusal clamps the identifiers it echoes and re-measures itself (`refusal_reply` / `enforce_frame_cap` in `agent_call.rs`). The `agent.query` surface was not touched by that change.

**Observed (by reading, not executed)**

- `handle_agent_query`'s refusals echo `resource` and `reqId` verbatim; nothing bounds them below the 8 MiB incoming frame cap, so a refusal built from a near-cap `resource` exceeds the cap on the way out.
- `spawn_agent_query` hands the resolved result to the writer with no size check, so a curated reply over the cap (unlikely today because the curated tools page or cap themselves, but not guaranteed) closes the socket.

**Expected**

Same treatment as `agent.call`: route `agent.query` refusals through the bounded refusal builder and measure the reply before writing, substituting `result_too_large`.

**Suggested fix**

Reuse `agent_call::refusal_reply`-style clamping for the query envelope and add an `enforce_frame_cap` call in `spawn_agent_query` (or the shared writer), with the same unit tests: a cap-sized `resource` yields a refusal that fits; a synthetic over-cap result is refused with the sentinel.

title: Dependabot auto-merge landed #1127 with a failing Tests check; require the test jobs before merge
body:
The dependabot PR #1127 (vitest group → 5.x) was merged into `main` although its own `🧪 Tests` check concluded **FAILURE**. Since that merge the root `pnpm test` fails on `main` (21 extension tests in `apps/extension/src/sidepanel/sidepanel.test.ts` and `src/background.test.ts`: listeners registered at module import are no longer captured under vitest 5), and because the pre-push hook runs the root suite, every branch's push is blocked until a hotfix lands.

**Severity**: high (process; blocks all pushes)
**Area**: repository automation — dependabot auto-merge flow and the required-checks set on `main`.

**Observed**

- `gh pr view 1127 --json statusCheckRollup`: `🧪 Tests: FAILURE`, `🤖 AI Review OK: SUCCESS`; PR state merged.
- `gh run list --branch main`: only Format Guard / Deploy Landing Page / Security / Quality ran on the merge commit; no test job gates the merge.

**Expected**

A dependabot PR that fails `🧪 Tests` must not auto-merge. Either add `🧪 Tests` (and the Rust test job) to the required status checks for `main`, or make the auto-merge workflow wait for those checks explicitly.

**Suggested fix**

- Branch protection / rulesets: require `🧪 Tests` (JS) and the Rust test job alongside `🤖 AI Review OK`.
- The auto-merge workflow (see the dependabot auto-merge workflow under `.github/workflows/`) should enable auto-merge only after the required checks are green, not on approval alone.
- A follow-up hotfix PR fixes the two extension test files for vitest 5.

title: MCP server roadmap: sourced opportunities from the 2026-09-07 research pass
body:
Research pass (2026-09-07) over the current MCP specification, client support, distribution channels, comparable servers and agent-tool guidance, mapped onto this app's MCP server (`ajh-tauri agent mcp`, ADR-040). Priorities are a proposal, not a decision; each item names what to build and where it fits.

## Landscape

Grounding: `mcp.rs` + ADR-040 are current as read — legacy 2025-11-25 JSON-RPC stdio, 6 curated read tools + 3 tiered `call-*` generic tools over `POLICY`, per-tool `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint`/`idempotentHint`/`openWorldHint` annotations (already correct), `_meta["anthropic/requiresUserInteraction"]` on `call-irreversible` only (already correct — `call-reversible` deliberately omits it), cursor pagination on `found-jobs` only, no resources/prompts/structuredContent/title/icons, discovered today only via a hand-copied Settings→Developer snippet.

Spec landscape (2026-07-28, the "modern era" ADR-040 named as a future follow-up): this is the largest MCP revision since launch — it removes the `initialize` handshake and sessions entirely, requires `server/discover`, replaces server-initiated Roots/Sampling/Logging with client-side alternatives (all three formally **deprecated**, 12-month window), and rebuilds elicitation as a client-retries-the-request "MRTR" pattern instead of a server-initiated call. Tasks graduated from experimental to a versioned extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`, poll-based). Crucially: **no shipped client speaks 2026-07-28 yet** — Claude Code 2.1.258 sends `protocolVersion` 2025-11-25, Codex 0.144.6 sends 2025-06-18, both still doing the classic handshake — so ADR-040's legacy-wire choice remains correct and nothing here should trigger a wire migration. On that same legacy wire, though, both target clients already declare form-mode elicitation capability (verified live in ADR-040's own captured transcripts) — a lever this server doesn't pull yet. MCP Apps (interactive widgets) is real and live in Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code and Goose since Jan 2026, but this app already has a native GUI, so it's a "someday" polish item, not core. ChatGPT/OpenAI Apps SDK is a dead end for this server specifically: ChatGPT only speaks remote streamable-HTTP MCP, never local stdio, so reaching it would mean standing up a hosted bridge that contradicts the app's local-first design — out of scope.

Distribution landscape: today this server is reachable only by a technical user hand-copying a CLI snippet. The real on-ramps the ecosystem actually uses are Claude Desktop `.mcpb` one-click bundles (which explicitly support wrapping a pre-built binary, not just node/python — precedent: BioMCP), Cursor's `cursor://…/mcp/install` and VS Code's `vscode://mcp/install` deeplinks (both just base64/URL-encode the same JSON config this app's Settings card already generates), and secondarily the official MCP Registry + community directories (PulseMCP, Glama) for discoverability. None of these exist yet for this server, and they're the biggest reach gap: they'd open Claude Desktop's *chat* surface (non-technical users asking "how's my job search going") in addition to the coding-agent-CLI audience this server currently serves exclusively.

Security landscape (tool poisoning, rug pulls, confused deputy) is almost entirely about a *malicious third-party* server — this app is the opposite risk shape (a trusted first-party server the user already installed, reading their own private data over a locally-authenticated bridge), so the sharp, applicable lessons are ones ADR-040 already implements (fence untrusted scraped text, gate destructive tiers behind explicit flags + annotations, never auto-resolve the confirm ceremony) rather than new work (cryptographic tool-description signing, hash-pinning against rug pulls) that targets a threat model this server doesn't have.

## Opportunities (priority 1 = first)

### P1 · Tool `title` + `icons` fields · effort S

**Why:** Every tool currently shows Claude Code/Cursor/VS Code users a raw snake-case `name` and nothing else. `title` (human display name, distinct from the programmatic `name`) and `icons` are both live, non-deprecated fields on the exact 2025-11-25 wire this server already speaks — zero wire risk, pure UI polish in every client's tool-approval and tool-list views.

**Build:** Add a `title` string (e.g. "Best Matches", "Run Autopilot Now") and a small `icons` array (data-URI or the app's existing icon asset) to each of the 9 static tool definitions in `mcp.rs` alongside the existing `annotations` block.

Sources: <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/server/tools> · <https://qaskills.sh/blog/mcp-server-testing-guide-2026>

### P2 · Cursor + VS Code one-click install deeplinks · effort S

**Why:** The Settings → Developer card already generates a copy-paste Claude Code/Codex registration snippet from the same binary path (`system_agent_cli_info`). Cursor and VS Code Copilot are two of the six target clients and both support a one-click `cursor://…/mcp/install?config=<base64 JSON>` / `vscode://mcp/install?<url-encoded JSON>` deeplink built from that identical config — currently unreached.

**Build:** Add "Add to Cursor" / "Add to VS Code" buttons next to the existing snippet in the Developer card, generating the deeplink client-side from the same JSON the card already builds.

Sources: <https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp/install-links> · <https://danywalls.com/create-one-click-mcp-installation-links-cursor-vscode>

### P3 · Claude Desktop `.mcpb` bundle · effort M

**Why:** This is the single biggest reach gap: every current distribution path (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code) is a coding-agent CLI. Claude Desktop is a chat surface non-technical job-searchers would actually use ("how's my search going today") and `.mcpb` explicitly supports wrapping a pre-built binary, not just node/python (precedent: BioMCP ships a compiled binary this way).

**Build:** Package the `agent mcp` mode (per-platform binary + manifest.json declaring the 6 curated read tools by default) as an `.mcpb`, ship it from the landing site / releases, and submit to Anthropic's Connectors Directory for broader discoverability.

## Not to build (and why)

Do not re-litigate what ADR-040 already decided with no new evidence: (1) stay on the legacy 2025-11-25 wire — confirmed again live, zero target clients (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code Copilot, Gemini CLI) speak 2026-07-28 yet; (2) never add `structuredContent` to PII-bearing tools — no observed client surfaces it and it would double every payload (résumé text, contact info, application records) in a persisted transcript for nothing. Additional things NOT to build right now: full protocol-level Tasks-extension machinery for `autopilot_run` — the app's own job-registry/persisted-status pattern (AGENTS.md rule 16) already gives MCP callers a call-now/poll-later shape without any wire change; a protocol Tasks handle would just duplicate it. Don't adopt Sampling — it's explicitly deprecated in the spec's own direction of travel, and this app already has its own AI-provider abstraction, which is the migration path the deprecation notice itself recommends. Don't chase ChatGPT/Apps-SDK distribution — stdio-only local servers are structurally unsupported there; only a hosted remote bridge would work, and that contradicts the local-first, no-cloud-relay design this app has kept deliberately. Don't adopt cryptographic tool-description signing/hash-pinning schemes aimed at third-party marketplace rug-pulls — this binary ships through the app's own signed installer/updater, a different (already-solved) trust chain. Don't over-invest in the MCP Apps/UI widget beyond one small prototype — the app already has a native GUI, so the ROI is chat-surface polish, worth confirming demand for (via the Claude Desktop bundle, priority 3) before building more.
